source.title: Mind the Gap: Examining the Self-Improvement Capabilities of Large Language Models
source.authors: Yu-Da Song; Hanlin Zhang; Carson Eisenach; S. Kakade; Dean P. Foster; Udaya Ghai

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how a generation-verification gap varies with model pre-training flops, not held-out cross-entropy loss, loss extrapolation, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its results therefore do not test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own scaling results for relative generation-verification gap (GV-gap), a different metric from the loss and allocation behaviors in the claim. Those findings are recorded as versions ["none"] and under fits_no_version. It does not report results on loss-law fits, predicting larger runs from smaller ones, architecture-shape effects, other modalities, or downstream predictability.
record.test_reason: The paper measures the generation-verification gap from self-verification reweighting and how it varies with pre-training flops. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss, loss extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture shape, or downstream-task predictability as a scaling claim. It invokes Kaplan et al. only as framing and future work. Its scaling result concerns a different construct and belongs under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Authors report that relative GV-gap grows monotonically with pre-training flops under certain verification methods (e.g. CoT-Score) for base models, not for absolute gap. They call the scaling analysis observational and propose a fuller Kaplan-style scaling study as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes self-improvement and GV-gap; it does not reproduce the loss-scaling or compute-optimal-allocation methods in the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The relative-gap trend is reported for certain verification methods. The paper says base-model results show the trend, whereas tested instruct-model families do not consistently show it; it also reports a temperature-1 exception for Qwen-1.5 14B.

fits_no_version.finding: With CoT-Score and similar verification, base models show relative GV-gap rising with log pre-training flops. The authors conjecture the rise is linear. The absolute gap shows no such trend (Fig. 12), instruct families mostly lack it (Fig. 9), and MC verification is non-monotonic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative self-verification gain of base LLMs grows roughly log-linearly with pre-training flops under stable verification methods.

record.problems: The authors characterize the scaling analysis as observational. The main plotted trends provide no uncertainty estimates, and the study measures GV-gap rather than the loss quantities in the claim.

untested.parts: All: no held-out pretraining loss measured.
All: no fits on small runs used to predict larger runs.
All: no parameter/token allocation under a fixed compute budget.
All: no shape variation at fixed parameter count.
All: no power-law fit in other modalities or regimes.
Downstream predictability. GSM8K/MATH generation accuracy across sizes is tabulated (Tables 4-5) only as context and is not analysed as a scaling or predictability result.
All: no loss-law exponents or allocation fits.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tranche and relation are right. Rows F1, F2, F5 and F6 have numeric values in Table 5 that the extraction missed. The Qwen-1.5 GSM8K CoT-S series is not strictly monotonic (7B dip), contrary to the authors' wording.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Whether loss-law fits on small runs predict much larger runs.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior for other modalities or training regimes.
Predictability of downstream task performance from scale or pretraining loss.
Dependence of loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting choices and setup.

rows.subject: Qwen-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Compared relative GV-gap across model sizes and pre-training flops.
rows.value: Increases monotonically with pre-training flops; numeric values are figure only.
rows.note: Family-level trend across sizes. This is a relative GV-gap result, not a held-out loss result.
rows.check: Value is not figure-only: Table 5 gives CoT-S (τ=8) relative gaps for 0.5B to 72B of -0.13, 3.10, 6.92, 5.50, 8.00, 8.40, 14.96. These dip at 7B, so the trend is not strictly monotonic as the row states. The state is not assessable against any claim version.
